absent: Locking and concurrency rules for shared boot video globals, heap and serial state are not shown.
Heap implementation, videocards section linkage and full boot parameter layout beyond referenced fields are not shown.
Serial programming beyond base variable and register offsets, including output path and line control, is not shown.
Firmware register block layout, BIOS call conventions and wakeup differences beyond mode restore are not shown.
Page table, CR3, PCID and FRED versus IDT table maintenance are not shown.
Timer rearm, instrumentation markers, warning behavior and KVM event type definitions are not shown.
Memory encryption key handling, SNP initialization detail and post enablement translation effects are not shown.
VESA protected mode interface use and palette programming beyond size reporting are not shown.

findings.text: Boot time confidential memory setup entry receives boot parameters, initializes guest SNP state, probes processor capability leaves, derives an encryption position mask, consults firmware status to select a personality, enforces consistency, applies SME gating, and on success publishes global masks plus vendor marker and narrows the physical address mask.

Activation is skipped when extended leaf support is below the required level, when neither capability bit is present, when SME lacks loader opt in, when hypervisor presence is observed, or when system configuration does not report encryption; mismatch between early SNP result and firmware SNP status terminates the guest.

Capability encoding uses bit 0 for memory encryption and bit 1 for virtualization protection; encryption bit position comes from low six bits of the companion capability word; firmware status selects the active personality and reports SNP enablement.
Boot page table helper accepts a table pointer and entry value and returns the entry unchanged, meaning no user table remapping is performed at this stage.

Boot string support offers byte comparison through memory comparison, signed conversion that negates unsigned parsing after a leading dash, a builtin memory comparison alias, a header guard, and an overflow marker using the top bit of a 32 bit word.
Early boot state includes a mutable integer holding the serial port base and a constant version string combining release, builder, host and version information.
Serial register layout uses offset 0 for transmit, offset 5 for line status, and value 0x20 as transmitter ready indication.

Packed firmware video types have no padding. A far pointer stores 16 bit offset then 16 bit segment. General controller information stores signature, version, vendor pointer, capabilities, mode list pointer, total memory and a large reserved tail.

Packed mode detail groups window attributes and geometry, addressing scheme, pitch, resolution, character cell, planes, bits per pixel, banking and layout codes, paging behavior, color mask sizes and positions with direct color detail, linear and offscreen addresses plus size, and a large reserved tail.

Controller signature equals little endian V E S A; presence needs successful firmware query plus matching signature plus version at least 0x0102; mode list ends at 0xffff and values above low nine bits are ignored.

Mode descriptor holds identifier, width, height and depth where zero means text, all 16 bit. Card descriptor holds name, mode set and probe callbacks, mode array, probed count, unsafe flag, and first plus count for unprobed modes that may still be tried. A macro places card descriptors in a dedicated retained section.

Mode number space uses 0x0000 menu, 0x0100 BIOS extended, 0x0200 VESA extended, 0x0900 V7, 0x0f00 to 0x0f09 specials covering 80x25, 8 point, 80x43, 80x28, current mode, 80x30, 80x34, 80x60, graphics hack and last special, 0x1000 resolution range and 0x8000 recalculation flag.
Adapter classes are 0 for CGA MDA HGC, 1 for EGA and 2 for VGA and later.

Shared boot video integers record detected adapter class, forced width and height overriding firmware queries, whether screen contents changed across a mode change, and whether linear framebuffer graphics mode is active.

BIOS mode handling programs a mode through firmware, rereads current mode ignoring the top bit, succeeds on match, otherwise tries to restore the entry mode outside wakeup context and reports failure while marking contents lost. Probing runs only on EGA or VGA, scans a fixed interval, skips duplicates and heap exhaustion, trial sets candidates, validates text behavior via controller and cursor state, records survivors with firmware supplied dimensions, restores the saved mode and returns survivor count.

VESA handling first queries controller state and stops unless firmware status, signature and version show presence. It then walks the firmware mode list to its terminator, skips exhaustion and out of range values, queries each mode, registers text modes with the required attribute pattern and, when framebuffer support is compiled in, single plane packed graphics modes with linear capability. Setting re queries the mode, separates text from graphics by attributes, requests linear addressing for graphics, programs the mode, then records text geometry and restore state or stores graphics parameters.

Graphics parameter commit marks linear framebuffer type and copies attributes, pitch, size, depth, planes, base, color layout, total memory, DAC sizes with zero offsets for low depth after opportunistically switching to eight bit DAC when advertised, and protected mode entry pointer when supplied.

VGA handling classifies hardware through firmware feature calls, records returned state and VGA marker outside wakeup context, then selects one of three static text tables with matching name and returns its length. Mode setting normalizes firmware mode to supported text values, forces dimensions from the descriptor, marks restore, and dispatches to font and scanline helpers for taller variants.

Static tables list 80 column text geometries: VGA has seven variants from 25 to 60 rows, EGA has two variants, CGA has one. Extended helpers adjust vertical timing and overflow, select scanline counts and fonts, and set cursor shape to reach 30, 34, 43, 50 and 60 row geometries.

Mode membership test scans every registered card and its probed modes for an equal identifier. Registrations retained in a dedicated section are BIOS with unsafe probing and 0x80 extended modes, VESA with 0x200 extended modes, and VGA with probe and set callbacks.
Boot video keeps a static 16 bit video segment and a saved screen record holding dimensions, cursor coordinates and a pointer to saved frame data.

Small video helpers provide a store macro delegating to screen save, an index tester that writes then reads a port index, and character helpers converting letters to nibbles and packing s c a n into one word.

Isolation encodings place the user table selector at page shift and the user context selector at the architecture user PCID bit, with one mask per selector plus their combination; a per CPU alias names the user flush mask field inside translation state.

Virtualization exit entry separates external interrupts from non maskable events. External interrupts dispatch through FRED on 64 bit or IDT on 32 bit, then around instrumentation rearm deferred timers to repair disabled interrupt context. Other events are expected to be non maskable and use FRED when available else the IDT non maskable path with interrupts disabled.

Low level helpers resolve an IDT vector to its gate address and enter with interrupts disabled, provide assembly trampolines for interrupt and non maskable entry with interrupts disabled, and provide a predictor barrier that programs the prediction command register from a shared value, refreshes return predictions and returns.

Mode enumeration stops silently when heap space is exhausted, BIOS probing is flagged unsafe and must only run after explicit scan consent, and a failed BIOS mode change can leave hardware in neither requested nor original state despite a revert attempt.

Video discovery trusts firmware for presence, mode lists, geometry and cursor state, so wrong firmware data yields missing or wrong modes; memory encryption setup trusts processor and firmware reports that a hostile hypervisor could influence apart from explicit hypervisor refusal and SNP mismatch abort.
